title: Week 10
priceNote: Prices are estimates from typical Aldi and Publix shelf prices and do not include tax. A Cajun and Creole week: blackened chicken and a pot of red beans with smoked sausage, plus this week's gumbo.
allergyNote: Nothing on this plan contains tree nuts or fish. Cajun seasoning, hot sauce and smoked sausage are normally nut-free, but check the labels for a 'may contain tree nuts' line if your allergy is strict.
weekendNote: Nothing is required this weekend. A bowl of Cajun chicken pasta is waiting for Saturday's lunch, and about 2 cups of red beans are in the freezer for a later week.
snacks: Cottage cheese with a drizzle of honey
String cheese and a couple of clementines

mon.heads: Red beans on a Monday is a New Orleans tradition, and the pot was made Sunday. Dinner makes Wednesday's lunch.

wed.heads: Tonight's new one is dinner for two and covers Thursday's lunch. Move the 3 frozen chicken portions to the fridge for Friday.

thu.heads: Dinner is a 10-minute skillet hash after pickleball.

fri.heads: Cajun chicken pasta for two tonight. It makes Saturday's lunch.

prep.title: Sunday batch prep
prep.makes: About 8 portions of blackened chicken, 6 cups of red beans, garlic rice, a tray of Cajun potatoes and green beans, Creole remoulade, 6 egg muffins and 2 jars of oats
steps: Start the red beans first so they simmer while everything else cooks.
Heat the oven to 425°F and rub the chicken with the Cajun spice.
Roast the chicken on one sheet pan and the potatoes on another, 25 minutes, swapping halfway. Add the green beans to the potato pan for the last 12 minutes.
Cook the garlic rice and stir the remoulade together.
Turn the oven down to 350°F and bake the egg muffins for 20 to 22 minutes.
Stir the oats together in 2 jars.
Slice the chicken and portion it: 5 in the fridge (Monday and Tuesday bowls, Tuesday's po'boy, 2 for Wednesday's gumbo).
Freeze the other 3 chicken portions (Friday's bowl and the pasta). Cooked chicken keeps 3 to 4 days, so the end of the week waits in the freezer.
Pack 2 chicken bowls.

prep.title: Wednesday night
prep.makes: Gumbo for two plus Thursday's lunch, with the end of the week ready
steps: Move the 3 frozen chicken portions to the fridge.
Make the gumbo and pack one bowl for Thursday.

blackened-chicken.name: Sheet-pan blackened chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the thighs with 2 tbsp olive oil, then rub them all over with 2 tbsp Cajun seasoning, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder and ½ tsp dried thyme.
Spread them on a sheet pan and roast 22 to 25 minutes, until they reach 175°F and the spice crust darkens.
Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Portion into 8 containers. Fridge 5, freeze 3.
blackened-chicken.tip: Blackened just means a dark, spicy crust. The oven does it without smoking up the kitchen.

red-beans.name: Big-pot red beans with smoked sausage
steps: Brown the sausage coins in 1 tbsp olive oil in a large pot, 4 minutes.
Add the diced onion, bell pepper and celery (the Cajun trinity) and cook 6 minutes until soft, then 4 minced garlic cloves, 2 tsp Cajun seasoning and 1 tsp dried thyme for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed beans, 2 cups broth and 2 bay leaves. Simmer 25 minutes, stirring now and then.
Mash about a cup of the beans against the side of the pot so the sauce turns creamy. Add a few dashes of hot sauce and remove the bay leaves.
Cool and refrigerate. Freeze about 2 cups for a later week.
red-beans.tip: Mashing some of the beans is the trick that makes red beans creamy without any butter.

garlic-rice.name: Garlic rice
steps: Sizzle 2 minced garlic cloves in 1 tbsp olive oil in the pot for 30 seconds.
Add 2 cups rice, 3 cups of water and 1 tsp salt. Cover and cook 15 minutes, then rest 5.
Fluff, cool and store. It keeps 5 days.

cajun-potatoes.name: Cajun roasted potatoes and green beans
steps: Toss the halved potatoes on a sheet pan with 1½ tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp Cajun seasoning and ½ tsp salt, and roast at 425°F for 25 minutes next to the chicken.
Toss the trimmed green beans with the last ½ tbsp oil and add them to the pan for the last 12 minutes.
Cool and store in one container.

remoulade.name: Creole yogurt remoulade
steps: Stir 1 cup Greek yogurt, 1 tbsp Dijon mustard, 2 tbsp dill pickle relish, 1 tsp hot sauce, the juice of half the lemon, 1 small grated garlic clove, 1 minced green onion and ½ tsp smoked paprika together.
Keeps 5 days in a jar.
remoulade.tip: Tangy, a little spicy and creamy. It is the sauce that makes a po'boy a po'boy.

egg-muffins.name: Sausage and cheddar egg muffins

ingredients.qty: the rest of the slices, torn

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and spray 6 muffin cups well.
Microwave the sausage patties 1 minute and crumble them.
Divide the sausage, torn cheddar, diced bell pepper and sliced green onions between the cups.
Whisk 7 eggs, ¼ cup milk and a pinch each of salt and black pepper and pour it over.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes until puffed and set. Reheat 2 for 40 seconds.
egg-muffins.tip: Uses up last week's eggs, sausage patties and cheddar.

foster-oats.name: Bananas foster overnight oats
steps: Mash one banana with 1 tbsp honey and ¾ tsp cinnamon.
Stir in 1 cup oats, 1 cup milk and ½ cup yogurt and split between 2 jars.
Refrigerate overnight. Top with the other banana, sliced, and the last ¼ tsp cinnamon in the morning.
foster-oats.tip: The New Orleans dessert in breakfast form, without the rum or the butter.

chicken-bowl.name: Blackened chicken bowl with remoulade
steps: Pack ¾ cup garlic rice, 1 cup Cajun potatoes and green beans and a portion of blackened chicken in each container, with the chopped tomato on the side.
Reheat the warm part 2 minutes.
Add the tomato, 2 tbsp Creole remoulade and a pinch of green onions.
chicken-bowl.tip: Friday's comes from the frozen portion you moved to the fridge Wednesday.

red-beans-rice.name: Red beans and rice
steps: Reheat the red beans 2 to 3 minutes, stirring once.
Spoon them over ¾ cup garlic rice (warm it 1 minute first) and finish with hot sauce to taste and green onions.
red-beans-rice.tip: The Monday tradition: it was once laundry day, and a pot of beans could simmer on its own.

poboys.name: Blackened chicken po'boy
steps: Crisp the chicken in a hot skillet, 3 minutes.
Split the roll and toast it cut side down in the same pan, 1 minute.
Spread both sides with 3 tbsp Creole remoulade, then pile on shredded lettuce, sliced tomato and chicken. Shake on a few dashes of hot sauce.
poboys.tip: A New Orleans sandwich in 10 minutes after pickleball.

gumbo.name: Chicken and sausage gumbo

ingredients.qty: half the second rope, in coins

steps: Make the roux: stir ⅓ cup flour and ⅓ cup olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, without stopping, until it is the color of peanut butter.
Add the diced onion, bell pepper and celery (it will sizzle) and cook 5 minutes, then 4 minced garlic cloves, 1 tbsp Cajun seasoning and 1 tsp dried thyme for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in 4 cups broth, then add the can of diced tomatoes with its juice, the frozen okra, the sausage coins and 2 bay leaves. Simmer 20 minutes.
Stir in 2 portions of shredded blackened chicken and simmer 5 more minutes. Add hot sauce to taste and remove the bay leaves.
Serve over ¾ cup garlic rice per bowl with green onions. Pack one bowl for Thursday.
gumbo.tip: This week's new one. The roux is the whole secret: keep stirring and stop at peanut-butter brown for a deep, toasty flavor. The okra thickens it too.

red-bean-hash.name: Red bean and potato hash with fried eggs
steps: Crisp the chopped Cajun potatoes and green beans in 1 tsp olive oil in a hot cast iron, 4 minutes, pressing them down.
Add 1 cup red beans and the corn and heat through, 2 minutes.
Make 2 wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook 3 minutes until the whites set.
Finish with a few dashes of hot sauce and green onions.

cajun-pasta.name: Creamy Cajun chicken pasta with garlic rolls

ingredients.qty: the other half rope, in coins
the last one and a half, sliced

steps: Boil the linguine in salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
Meanwhile, brown the sausage in 1 tbsp oil, 3 minutes. Add the sliced bell peppers and onion for 5 minutes, then 3 minced cloves of garlic and 2 tsp Cajun seasoning for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in 1 tbsp flour, then slowly stir in 1½ cups milk and simmer 2 minutes until it thickens. Off the heat, stir in ½ cup yogurt and ¾ cup parmesan.
Toss in the linguine and the sliced blackened chicken until coated.
Brush the 2 split rolls with the last tbsp of oil mixed with the last clove of garlic, grated, and toast them cut side down in a skillet, 2 minutes.
Top the pasta with green onions. Pack one bowl for Saturday.
cajun-pasta.tip: Made from the frozen chicken you moved to the fridge Wednesday. The yogurt goes in off the heat so it stays creamy.
